findings: Exact gate ties occur in real prompts: the 6th and 7th biased expert scores are equal (margin 0.0) at some rows, for example p1 layers 2, 36 and 37. torch.topk picks among them in an unspecified order, so router comparisons must exclude exact ties and report near ties (run.json near_ties).

Cached decode and one-shot replay of the same fixed sequence differ in the reference itself: logits by about 1 to 5 in absolute value, residual streams by up to 2,048 at layer 39, and one argmax (e-window-127, g4) flips. Compare Psionic decode against reference decode and replay against replay; the decode-replay gap is a floor for tolerances, not a target.
All 40 layers run on every decode step; no layer is skipped after prefill (residual hashes exist for all 40 layers at all 33 steps).
not_done: A multi-token chunk after position 0 is not possible in the reference (decode paths assume one token), so the chunked mode prefills half the prompt and then steps one token at a time.
